meta.description: Master gazetteer for the Undercity - all districts, underground locations, and establishments

ring_structure.name: Tower Core
ring_structure.description: The Tower of Last Chance itself. Restricted access.

ring_structure.name: Grand Forum Ring
ring_structure.description: Administrative heart. Archives, courts, guild HQs.

ring_structure.name: Sanctum Ring
ring_structure.description: Religious and scholarly. Temples, academies, research.

ring_structure.name: Residential Ring
ring_structure.description: Where most citizens live. Middle to lower class.

ring_structure.name: Outer Ring
ring_structure.description: Industrial, military, Warrens pockets. The edge.

Tower of Last Chance.description: The ancient semi-sentient structure at the heart of the Undercity. The Oracle dwells within.

sub_areas.name: The Oracle Chamber
sub_areas.description: Where the Oracle speaks to those deemed worthy

sub_areas.name: The Great Beam
sub_areas.description: Energy column rising from the Tower apex, visible everywhere

sub_areas.name: Archival Vaults
sub_areas.description: Deep storage of records the Tower Authority deems sensitive

places_of_interest.name: The Resonance Steps
places_of_interest.description: Stone stairs leading to the Tower entrance that hum faintly with arcane energy. Suppliants wait here for days.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Casting detect magic here reveals an overwhelming aura of divination and conjuration

places_of_interest.name: The First Gate
places_of_interest.description: Massive sealed gate of unknown alloy. No key exists. It opens only for the Oracle's chosen.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Knock and arcane lock spells have no effect

parks.name: The Moat Garden
parks.description: Narrow bioluminescent garden ringing the Tower base. Maintained by Tower Authority. Public access permitted.
features: warding glyphs etched into the path

Grand Forum.description: The open plaza at the city's political heart. Public announcements, political maneuvering, information brokers.

sub_areas.name: Petitioner's Steps
sub_areas.description: Where citizens wait for audience with officials

notable_establishments.name: The Gilded Quill
notable_establishments.description: Upscale establishment favored by diplomats and info brokers

notable_establishments.name: Grand Forum Library
notable_establishments.description: Guild of Ashen Scrolls main archive

places_of_interest.name: The Proclamation Pillars
places_of_interest.description: Seven stone pillars carved with every major law passed since the city's founding. Lawyers and archivists gather here to argue interpretations.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: comprehend languages reveals older edicts in three extinct dialects

places_of_interest.name: The Forum Clock
places_of_interest.description: A massive mechanical timepiece suspended above the plaza, powered by arcane clockwork. The only public clock in Ring 1.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: mending keeps it running; it has resisted dispel magic for 80 years

places_of_interest.name: The Sorrow Wall
places_of_interest.description: A long marble wall etched with the names of every citizen who died in a Rift event. New names are added weekly.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: speak with dead cast near the wall sometimes produces unexpected responses

small_shops.name: The Gilded Quill Trading Post
small_shops.description: Maps, dungeon survey reports, and Rift zone charts sold by verified brokers.
small_shops.dnd_relevance: maps grant advantage on Survival checks in charted areas

small_shops.name: Forum Cartographers
small_shops.description: Custom survey maps of any district. Warden-certified accuracy guaranteed.
small_shops.dnd_relevance: grants proficiency-equivalent navigation in mapped area for 24h

small_shops.name: The Notary's Stall
small_shops.description: Document authentication, contract witnessing, and official seal application.
small_shops.dnd_relevance: contract scrolls are legally enforceable under city law

parks.name: The Forum Garden
parks.description: A formal garden of cultivated underground fungi and dome-lit flower beds at the plaza's east edge. Diplomatic meetings often happen on its stone benches.
features: stone fountain with purified canal water

parks.name: The Petitioner's Grove
parks.description: A small bioluminescent garden where those awaiting audience sit. Maintained by Tower Authority as a gesture of civility.

malls.name: The Forum Arcade
malls.description: A covered colonnade of high-end shops lining the Forum's northern face. The most prestigious commercial address in the city.
malls.specialty: Political services, legal instruments, and luxury information goods

Guild Spires.description: Towering faction headquarters. The Adventurers Guild, Merchant Guild, and Artificers make their homes here.

sub_areas.name: Adventurers Guild Hall
sub_areas.description: Mission board, registration, Mari Fen's desk

sub_areas.name: Silver Spire
sub_areas.description: Aric Veyne's tower, SS-Rank adventurer residence

places_of_interest.name: The Champion's Plinth
places_of_interest.description: A rotating magical display case at the Spires base showing the current top-ranked adventurers' likenesses in glowing illusion-craft.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Ranked adventurers can request one free identify per month at the Artificers Collective

places_of_interest.name: The Artificers Certification Wall
places_of_interest.description: A floor-to-ceiling board displaying every certified magic item in the city registry. Updated daily by junior artificers.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Successful Investigation DC 14 locates any item in registry; items here can be legally purchased

places_of_interest.name: The Merchant Exchange Bell
places_of_interest.description: An enormous bronze bell rung to open and close official trade sessions. Its tone carries to Ring 3.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Thieves who steal from within earshot during bell hours face doubled Warden response time penalties

small_shops.name: Sigil & Seal
small_shops.description: Arcane focuses, spell component pouches, and certified wondrous items for Guild-registered adventurers.
small_shops.dnd_relevance: arcane focus, spell components, ring of protection, cloak of elvenkind

small_shops.name: The Prospect's Outfitter
small_shops.description: Budget adventuring gear for new Guild registrants. Everything a D-rank needs for their first mission.
small_shops.dnd_relevance: dungeoneer's pack, healer's kit, 50ft rope

small_shops.name: The Ranking Notary
small_shops.description: Official registration, rank appeals, and mission contract authentication.
small_shops.dnd_relevance: contracts are required for any mission above E-rank pay grade

parks.name: The Spires Terrace
parks.description: An elevated plaza between the Spire towers with imported stone benches and dome-filtered pale light. Used for off-duty Guild socializing.

malls.name: The Spires Concourse
malls.description: A multi-level commercial gallery at the base of the Guild Spires, catering exclusively to registered Guild members and faction representatives.
malls.specialty: Adventuring equipment, magical certification, and Guild-only services

Archive Row.description: Glass Sigil territory. Libraries, scriptoriums, and the accumulated knowledge of ages.

sub_areas.name: Grand Archive Dome
sub_areas.description: Main Glass Sigil repository under the great glass dome

sub_areas.name: The Cataloguing Halls
sub_areas.description: Where junior archivists sort incoming materials

places_of_interest.name: The Grand Archive Dome
places_of_interest.description: The great glass dome itself — the largest single structure in Ring 1 aside from the Tower. The dome is Sigil-made and partially transparent, casting archival light within.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Any Arcana or History check made inside the Dome gains a +2 bonus from ambient reference access

places_of_interest.name: The Index Fountain
places_of_interest.description: A shimmering liquid-crystal fountain in the Archive courtyard that displays the day's new acquisitions as floating text. Archivists check it every morning.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Successful Arcana DC 12 can query the index for a specific topic; one free query per day per visitor

places_of_interest.name: The First Record Stone
places_of_interest.description: The oldest surviving written record in the city — a slab of inscribed basalt behind glass in the Archive lobby.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: comprehend languages required to read the archaic dialect; reveals pre-Tower city history

small_shops.name: The Cataloguing Hand
small_shops.description: Scrolls of Identify, detect magic, comprehend languages, and remove curse. All Glass Sigil certified.
small_shops.dnd_relevance: identify scroll, detect magic, comprehend languages, remove curse

small_shops.name: Scribe's Supply
small_shops.description: Writing materials, preservation wax, blank scroll stock, and enchanted inks for scribing.
small_shops.dnd_relevance: required for scribing any spell scroll

small_shops.name: The Pressed Page
small_shops.description: Rare book dealer operating under Glass Sigil charter. Spell theory, dungeon survey records, and faction histories.
small_shops.signature_item: Dungeon survey record (any known dungeon, DC 15 to find specific)
small_shops.dnd_relevance: grants advantage on Intelligence checks related to surveyed dungeon

parks.name: The Archive Courtyard
parks.description: A serene enclosed garden between the archive wings. Quiet reading alcoves, stone tables, and a preservation-ward that keeps insects and moisture out.
features: reading alcoves with pale dome light

parks.name: The Memory Walk
parks.description: A long covered colonnade planted with crystalline memory-flowers that glow faintly when walked past. Archivists believe the flowers absorb and hold emotional impressions.

malls.name: The Row Arcade
malls.description: A scholarly shopping hall along Archive Row's main street. Frequented by researchers, scribes, and serious collectors.
malls.specialty: Scrolls, books, magical research materials, and scribe supplies

Diplomats Row.description: Embassy buildings and neutral meeting grounds for inter-faction negotiations.

places_of_interest.name: The Accord Statue
places_of_interest.description: A bronze statue of the seven founding faction signatories standing in a circle, hands extended toward the center. The plaque beneath reads: 'We agreed, once.'
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: A successful Insight DC 13 check reveals the statue was repaired after being vandalized — one figure's hand was removed and reattached

places_of_interest.name: The Neutral Hall Crystal
places_of_interest.description: A floating truth-crystal above the Neutral Hall table that glows red if a speaker is knowingly lying. All major negotiations happen beneath it.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Functions as a permanent zone of truth (DC 16 Will save to resist) during active negotiations

places_of_interest.name: The Condolence Board
places_of_interest.description: A velvet-lined message board in the embassy corridor where factions post formal condolences after inter-faction deaths. Etiquette dictates specific mourning language.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Studying the board with History DC 14 reveals a pattern — some factions post condolences before deaths are publicly announced

small_shops.name: The Neutral Ground Armourers
small_shops.description: Ceremonial arms and formal armour for diplomatic functions. Looks dangerous, designed for display.
small_shops.dnd_relevance: +1 longsword, formal armor sets

small_shops.name: The Courier's Table
small_shops.description: Diplomatic message delivery service with guaranteed discretion. Neutral faction affiliation.
small_shops.dnd_relevance: tamper-evident wax seal uses a 2nd-level alarm effect

parks.name: The Garden of Accord
parks.description: Formal diplomatic gardens maintained under strict neutrality treaty. All factions contribute one groundskeeper each. The only place in the city where faction members are forbidden from faction insignia.

Sanctum Quarter.description: Major temples and religious administration. Serpent Choir's seat of power.

sub_areas.name: Choir Hall
sub_areas.description: Serpent Choir headquarters, High Apostle Yzura's seat

notable_establishments.name: Vesper's Consultation Office
notable_establishments.description: Contract Mediator Vesper sees petitioners here

notable_establishments.name: Tithe House
notable_establishments.description: Where divine contracts are finalized and payments rendered

places_of_interest.name: The Contract Obelisk
places_of_interest.description: A 30-foot obelisk in the Sanctum plaza engraved with the terms of the Founding Divine Compact — the agreement that allows the Choir to operate in the Undercity. The Choir polishes it weekly.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Any cleric who meditates here for 10 minutes gains one additional use of Channel Divinity that day

places_of_interest.name: The Penitent's Gate
places_of_interest.description: A golden archway at the Choir Hall entrance. Those who pass through who have broken a Choir contract feel a burning sensation; those who have honored all contracts feel warmth.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Functions as detect evil and good for Choir contract status when characters pass through

places_of_interest.name: The Tithe Pool
places_of_interest.description: A circular pool of still water in the plaza where citizens drop coins when making informal prayers. The Choir skims it daily and claims it funds good works.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Coins left for 24h become mildly blessed; function as holy water when used in rituals (half strength)

small_shops.name: The Root & Residue
small_shops.description: Holy water, sacred incense, diamond dust for revivify, and genuine spell components sourced under Choir contract.
small_shops.dnd_relevance: holy water, revivify components, spell components, cure wounds

small_shops.name: The Pilgrim's Rest Infirmary
small_shops.description: Short-rest healing services: lay on hands surrogates, lesser restoration, and cure wounds at tiered Guild rates.
small_shops.dnd_relevance: cure wounds, lesser restoration, healing services

small_shops.name: The Contract Scribe's Table
small_shops.description: Divine contract scribing for personal oaths and binding agreements. Witnessed and warded by Choir scribes.
small_shops.dnd_relevance: binding contracts enforceable by zone of truth effect

parks.name: The Pantheon Gardens
parks.description: A formal garden lining Pantheon Walk between the temples. Each deity's section is planted with symbolically appropriate flora — death's domain grows nightshade, healing's domain grows silverleaf.

parks.name: The Quiet Terrace
parks.description: A rooftop garden above the Pilgrim's Rest for convalescent patients. Guarded against noise by a permanent silence ward on the perimeter.

malls.name: The Sanctum Colonnade
malls.description: A covered shopping gallery along the Sanctum's eastern face where religious goods, healing supplies, and ritual materials are sold. All vendors are Choir-approved.
malls.specialty: Divine spell components, healing services, and ritual goods

Temple Row.description: Cathedral of the Eternal Flame, Temple of the Silent Watch, Shrine of Forgotten Names.

sub_areas.name: Cathedral of the Eternal Flame
sub_areas.description: Tallest religious structure, sacred fire never extinguished

sub_areas.name: Shrine of Forgotten Names
sub_areas.description: Memorial to those lost to Rifts

places_of_interest.name: The Eternal Flame
places_of_interest.description: The sacred fire in the Cathedral that has not been extinguished in recorded history. A fire elemental of great age is said to be bound within it.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Fire damage dealt within 30ft of the flame is maximized once per short rest for fire-domain clerics

places_of_interest.name: Shrine of Forgotten Names
places_of_interest.description: A wall of stone tiles, each bearing the name of a citizen lost to Rift events. Families pay the Cathedral to add tiles. Tens of thousands of names.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: speak with dead cast adjacent to a tile may reach the named individual if no prior contact was attempted

places_of_interest.name: The Bell of Passage
places_of_interest.description: A massive bronze bell rung only for confirmed deaths of faction rank Senior or above. Its tone is heard across Ring 2 and parts of Ring 3.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: The bell's sound functions as a mild antimagic field for 10 minutes after ringing — no concentration spells

small_shops.name: Cathedral of the Eternal Flame — Alms Office
small_shops.description: Free lesser restoration for the genuinely destitute. Greater restoration by appointment. Brings your contract record.
small_shops.dnd_relevance: lesser restoration, greater restoration, remove curse

small_shops.name: The Flame Keeper's Candle Shop
small_shops.description: Blessed candles, sacred oils, and holy water in small quantities. Run by junior clerics. Practical and unpretentious.
small_shops.signature_item: Holy water (flask, 25 EC), blessed candle (ritual use)
small_shops.dnd_relevance: holy water, sacred flame cantrip-infused candles, ceremony spell components

parks.name: The Flame Garden
parks.description: A firelit garden directly behind the Cathedral maintained with perpetual torch-bushes — plants that grow small flames instead of flowers due to proximity to the Eternal Flame's aura.

parks.name: The Silent Watch Cloister
parks.description: A meditative courtyard maintained by the monks of the Silent Watch. Open to all but enforced silence within. The stonework mutes sound naturally.

Academy Heights.description: Wizards Tower, magical education, and arcane research facilities.

places_of_interest.name: The Arcane Manifold
places_of_interest.description: A permanent magical phenomenon at the Academy's center — a slow-rotating sphere of layered arcane energies hovering 40 feet above the courtyard. It has been there since the Academy's founding.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Within 30ft, spell save DC is increased by 1; detect magic reveals an incomprehensible web of conjuration, divination, and abjuration

places_of_interest.name: The Walk of Graduates
places_of_interest.description: A stone-flagged path lined with plaques naming every Archmage-certified graduate since founding. Gaps in the sequence mark those whose plaques were removed.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: History DC 14 identifies removed graduates and the reason for removal — mostly involving catastrophic experiments

places_of_interest.name: The Golem Yard
places_of_interest.description: An outdoor area where student-built golems are tested. Failures are left as warnings. There are seventeen failed golems in various states of arrested motion.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: At least two appear functional but remain motionless — Arcana DC 16 to determine why

small_shops.name: Reagent Row Collective
small_shops.description: Full spell component inventory operated by licensed suppliers. Bat guano, diamond dust, rare inks, powdered iron. Pre-order for unusual materials.
small_shops.dnd_relevance: spell components, arcane focus, ritual casting supplies

small_shops.name: The Resonant Mark
small_shops.description: Weapon and armour enchantments by licensed Wizards Tower artificers. +1 to +3 upgrades, elemental damage infusions.
small_shops.dnd_relevance: +1 weapons, +2 weapons, flaming/frost/lightning weapon infusion

small_shops.name: Academy Bookbindery
small_shops.description: Spell scribing services, blank spell books, and pre-written spell scrolls. Student pricing available.
small_shops.dnd_relevance: spellbook, spell scroll scribing

parks.name: The Academy Courtyard
parks.description: A broad stone courtyard around the Arcane Manifold. Students eat, argue, and practice cantrips here. The ambient magic means plants grow unusually — twisted but lush.

parks.name: The Research Gardens
parks.description: A rooftop garden used for outdoor spellwork experiments. Some sections are roped off permanently following incidents.
features: restricted sections with visible burn marks

malls.name: Reagent Row
malls.description: The main commercial strip of Academy Heights. Every shop services the magical trade — components, equipment, books, and enchantments. Busiest before exam periods.
malls.specialty: Arcane components, magical equipment, and enchantment services

The Reliquary.description: Sacred items studied and stored under heavy guard and wards.

places_of_interest.name: The Display Halls
places_of_interest.description: The public exhibition wing. Twenty approved artifacts behind glass and ward-walls. Most powerful items are represented only by replicas; the originals are elsewhere.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Arcana DC 16 distinguishes replicas from originals; one item in the current exhibition is authentic

places_of_interest.name: The Ward Lattice
places_of_interest.description: The Reliquary's outer security system — a visible lattice of blue-gold magical wards woven over the building's surface. Any theft attempt within 100ft triggers a silent alarm to Choir and Sigil guard posts.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: antimagic field, alarm, and glyph of warding effects layer the exterior

places_of_interest.name: The Study Antechamber
places_of_interest.description: A waiting room where approved researchers register before entering the Study Chambers. Decorated with framed letters of rejection from famous scholars denied access.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Persuasion DC 20 or formal Sigil sponsorship required for Study Chamber access

small_shops.name: Ashen Relics & Curios
small_shops.description: Sanctioned artifact appraisal and limited sale under Glass Sigil charter. Rings of mind shielding, necklaces of adaptation, and cleared wondrous items.
small_shops.dnd_relevance: ring of mind shielding, necklace of adaptation, wondrous items

small_shops.name: The Relic Appraiser
small_shops.description: Official Glass Sigil appraisal service. Identifies and values recovered magic items for a fee. All results are logged in the Sigil registry.
small_shops.dnd_relevance: identify, magic item appraisal, curse detection

parks.name: The Reliquary Forecourt
parks.description: A small formal garden at the Reliquary entrance with ward-marker sculptures and a shallow reflecting pool. The ward markers are functional, not decorative.

Cult Corners.description: Brother Thane's Meeting Hall and other smaller faiths operate here.

sub_areas.name: Brother Thane's Meeting Hall
sub_areas.description: Public gathering space for the Returned

places_of_interest.name: The Returned Board
places_of_interest.description: A public noticeboard outside Thane's Meeting Hall with testimonials from the Returned — those who claim to have died and come back. Updated weekly with new entries.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Investigation DC 11 finds inconsistencies in the death descriptions that suggest not all 'Returned' actually died

places_of_interest.name: Minor Shrine Row
places_of_interest.description: A street of small shrines to twelve obscure or suppressed deities. Most are under a foot tall, shoved into wall niches. A few have fresh offerings.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Religion DC 15 to identify any specific deity; three of the shrines are to gods the Serpent Choir officially banned

places_of_interest.name: The Vigil Fire
places_of_interest.description: A low perpetual flame in a clay bowl at the entrance to the Vigil House. Cult members who pass it touch it briefly. The fire has never gone out — cult members claim it is divine. Investigation suggests an enchanted ceramic.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Arcana DC 12 identifies a permanent prestidigitation effect; it is not divine

small_shops.name: The Offering Table
small_shops.description: Religious supplies for minor cults and personal shrine practice. Ritual candles, offering bowls, bone fragments, and burial herbs.
small_shops.dnd_relevance: ceremony spell components, funeral rites, speak with dead preparations

small_shops.name: The Returned's Closet
small_shops.description: Second-hand clothing and equipment from cult members who donated worldly possessions. Cheap but unpredictable inventory.
small_shops.signature_item: Random common magic item (donated, 50 EC, no guarantee)
small_shops.dnd_relevance: common magic items, random gear

parks.name: The Quiet Corner Garden
parks.description: A small unmaintained garden between two shrine buildings. Volunteers from the Patchwork Saints occasionally clear it. The cult uses it for outdoor vigils.

Cobbleway Market.description: Traditional open-air bazaar. Spice Alley, Cloth Row, street food stalls.

sub_areas.name: Food Court
sub_areas.description: Street food from a hundred cultures

places_of_interest.name: The Old Market Bell Tower
places_of_interest.description: A weathered stone tower above the market entrance whose bell marks the opening and closing of trade each day. The clock face shows only three hours because the fourth was damaged in a Rift event and never repaired.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: The tower's base has a concealed access hatch (Perception DC 14) used by smugglers to reach the Market Undercroft

places_of_interest.name: Spice Alley Mural
places_of_interest.description: A long mosaic mural on the Spice Alley wall depicting the founding of the market. Notable: one section was repainted and the original image — showing a now-banned faction — is visible under certain light angles.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Perception DC 13 in low light or with darkvision reveals the original banned faction sigil

places_of_interest.name: The Living Scale
places_of_interest.description: A massive enchanted scale at the market entrance, seven feet tall. Designed to detect tampering with goods sold in the market. Merchants avoid it; customers love it.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Functions as a truth-detector for trade goods — detects poison, magical alteration, or significant misrepresentation of weight

small_shops.name: Elune's Apothecary
small_shops.description: Potions of healing in bulk, herbal remedies, herbalism kit supplies, and poisons for professional use.
small_shops.signature_item: Potion of Healing (bulk rate: 45 EC each, min 4)
small_shops.dnd_relevance: potions of healing, herbalism kit, antitoxin, healer's kit

small_shops.name: The Cloth Row Tailor
small_shops.description: Custom-fitted adventuring clothes and disguise kits. Faction insignia removal and reapplication service. No questions on the insignia work.
small_shops.dnd_relevance: disguise kit, custom clothing with hidden pockets

small_shops.name: The Spice Merchant's Guild Stall
small_shops.description: Aromatic spices with legitimate uses — and some that serve double duty as ritual components or alchemical reagents.
small_shops.signature_item: Exotic spell component (disguised as spice, Perception DC 13 to identify)
small_shops.dnd_relevance: spell components, alchemist's supplies ingredients

parks.name: The Market Square Garden
parks.description: A chaotic burst of street-garden in the market's center — vendors sell cut flowers here and someone long ago planted a mushroom grove that now takes up a third of the space. Everyone works around it.
features: cut flower stalls on the perimeter

malls.name: The Cobbleway Grand Market Hall
malls.description: The main covered section of the market — a vaulted stone hall with stalls on three levels, accessed through the market gate. Oldest commercial structure in Ring 3.
malls.specialty: Daily goods, food, clothing, and consumable supplies for the whole city

Markets Infinite.description: The sprawling commercial heart of the city. Iron Fang Consortium territory.

notable_establishments.name: Sera Voss's Storage Room
notable_establishments.description: Behind a spice merchant, where Sera conducts business

places_of_interest.name: The Consortium Weigh Station
places_of_interest.description: An enormous public weigh station at Markets Infinite's entrance where all bulk goods are officially weighed and taxed. Iron Fang officers collect the tariff. Avoiding this station is technically smuggling.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Sleight of Hand DC 17 to pass significant contraband; failure triggers Iron Fang detention

places_of_interest.name: The TowerBay Depot Sign
places_of_interest.description: The largest illuminated commercial sign in the city — a 30-foot neon glyph visible from Ring 4 on a clear day. The Iron Fang Consortium commissioned it as a territorial marker as much as advertising.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Navigation within 5 miles of Markets Infinite is at advantage when the sign is visible

places_of_interest.name: The Crimson Alley Mural
places_of_interest.description: An unofficial mural at Crimson Alley's entrance showing the Iron Fang's version of their own history. Suspiciously heroic. Notable for what it omits.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: History DC 12 identifies four major Iron Fang crimes omitted from the mural

small_shops.name: Relic Row Outfitters
small_shops.description: Full adventuring kits, explorer's packs, and consignment magic items. Everything identified by a licensed scribe.
small_shops.dnd_relevance: explorer's pack, dungeoneer's pack, identify scroll, consignment magic items

small_shops.name: The Iron Coin Exchange
small_shops.description: Money changing, currency conversion, and EC-to-Kharma exchange at rates controlled by the Consortium. Not the best rates, but the safest.
small_shops.dnd_relevance: EC/Kharma exchange at posted rates

small_shops.name: Acquisition Solutions
small_shops.description: Iron Fang front for 'procurement services'. If you need something sourced without questions, this is the stall. High prices, reliable delivery.
small_shops.dnd_relevance: magic items, rare gear, restricted goods available with Gold or above faction standing

malls.name: Markets Infinite Central Hall
malls.description: The largest single commercial structure in the Undercity — a vaulted iron-and-stone hall nearly half a mile long. Six hundred registered vendor stalls. The Iron Fang controls all lease agreements.
malls.specialty: Everything. If it exists in the Undercity, it has been sold here.

malls.name: The Crimson Arcade
malls.description: A premium annexe attached to the main hall with higher-end Iron Fang sanctioned goods. Velvet ropes at the entrance and Consortium guards inside.
malls.specialty: High-value goods, rare acquisitions, and consortium-brokered specialty sales

Floating Bazaar.description: Elevated neon-lit platforms. Luxury goods, tourist attractions, sky restaurants.

sub_areas.name: Sky Platforms
sub_areas.description: Floating commercial platforms lit with neon

sub_areas.name: Vista Dining
sub_areas.description: Restaurants with views of the Tower

places_of_interest.name: The Tower View Platform
places_of_interest.description: The highest publicly accessible point in the Bazaar. A reinforced observation deck facing the Tower. Citizens come here to watch the Great Beam's nightly pulse.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Concentration spells cast here during the Beam's pulse have their duration doubled once per long rest

places_of_interest.name: The Suspension Walk
places_of_interest.description: A glass-floored bridge between two sky platforms with nothing but city below. A hundred feet long. Popular for dares and one confirmed murder.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Creatures with Acrophobia or fear of heights must succeed DC 12 Wisdom save to cross without hesitation

places_of_interest.name: The Tether & Claw
places_of_interest.description: The Bazaar's famous exotic animal handler — the only place in the city where familiars and exotic companions are sold openly and legally.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: find familiar spell component purchase, pseudodragon (with paperwork), exotic mounts

small_shops.name: The Tether & Claw
small_shops.description: Familiars, bonded mounts, and arcane companions. Current stock: ravens, owls, weasels, and a pseudodragon with incomplete paperwork.
small_shops.dnd_relevance: find familiar, pseudodragon, animal companion, exotic mounts

small_shops.name: Skylight Luxuries
small_shops.description: High-end fashion, exotic textiles, and luxury goods for Ring 1-2 buyers slumming in Ring 3.
small_shops.signature_item: Cloak of Billowing (cosmetic magic item, popular)
small_shops.dnd_relevance: cosmetic magic items, disguise materials, luxury clothing

small_shops.name: The Vista Provisions
small_shops.description: Expensive food and drink for the sky restaurants. Also sells bottled dome-rain water and platform-grown mushroom delicacies.
small_shops.signature_item: Bottled dome rain (novelty, blessed by Cathedral of Flame, 5 EC)
small_shops.dnd_relevance: holy water equivalent (very weak), gourmet spell component substitutes

parks.name: The Sky Garden
parks.description: A floating platform converted entirely to a garden. Maintained by a consortium of wealthy independent merchants as a status symbol. Free public access on the last day of each month.
features: the only outdoor café in Ring 3

malls.name: The Promenade
malls.description: The main elevated shopping walkway of the Floating Bazaar. Glass-and-neon aesthetic, upscale vendors, and a dress code that is technically not enforced but practically is.
malls.specialty: Luxury goods, exotic companions, and upscale dining experiences

Neon Row.description: Entertainment district. Taverns, theaters, pleasure houses. Never sleeps.

places_of_interest.name: The Neon Strip
places_of_interest.description: The main drag of Neon Row — half a mile of neon-glyph lit establishments, never dark, never quiet. The Obsidian Lotus controls the eastern end; independents control the western.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Bright light condition along the entire Strip; darkvision provides no advantage here even at night

places_of_interest.name: The Velvet Curtain Stage
places_of_interest.description: The city's premier playhouse. Current production has been running for seven months — a fictionalized account of a famous adventurer's death that the real adventurer's family contests legally.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Performance checks made on this stage have DC reduced by 3 due to quality acoustics and lighting

places_of_interest.name: The Vice Quarter's Corner
places_of_interest.description: The edge of the Vice Quarter where Lotus control begins. An invisible line in the pavement that everyone in Neon Row can point to exactly. Crossing it means Lotus rules apply.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Obsidian Lotus agents have advantage on Perception checks to notice newcomers entering their territory

small_shops.name: The Laughing Skull Supply
small_shops.description: Adventurer supplies attached to the bar. Rope, torches, rations, and questionable healing potions sold cheap. The bartender knows their limitations.
small_shops.dnd_relevance: potions of healing, torches, adventuring basics

small_shops.name: Blight & Brew
small_shops.description: Antitoxins, potions of resistance, and elixirs of health. Open all night because poison doesn't keep business hours.
small_shops.dnd_relevance: antitoxin, potion of resistance, elixir of health

small_shops.name: The Memory Den Supply
small_shops.description: Obsidian Lotus-adjacent shop selling memory-altering services and related supplies. Also offers dust of disappearance and smokepowder for professionals.
small_shops.dnd_relevance: dust of disappearance, smokepowder, stealth aids

parks.name: The Strip Atrium
parks.description: A narrow neon-lit park-like space between two theater buildings — benches, artificial vines grown with prestidigitation, and the permanent smell of entertainment-district food. Used by performers between acts.

malls.name: The Entertainment Quarter Complex
malls.description: A covered multi-level entertainment hub at Neon Row's center. Theaters, bars, shops, and back-room services on four levels. The Lotus controls the basement and sub-basement.
malls.specialty: Entertainment, consumables, vice, and night-market goods

Night Pits.description: Blood sport arenas. Gambling, gladiator culture, Sable's territory.

notable_establishments.name: Sable's Office
notable_establishments.description: Night Pits boss operates from here

notable_establishments.name: Champion's Obelisk
notable_establishments.description: Names of arena champions carved in stone

places_of_interest.name: The Grand Pit
places_of_interest.description: The main arena — a deep stone pit that seats four thousand, with tiered standing room for another two. Fights happen every day except the new moon. The crowd noise is audible from Ring 4.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Gladiators who fight here successfully three times gain a reputation bonus — Persuasion and Intimidation +2 in Rings 3-4

places_of_interest.name: Champion's Obelisk
places_of_interest.description: A twelve-foot obelisk outside the Grand Pit entrance with every champion's name carved in the stone in order of win count. Current champion is listed twice under two different names.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Investigation DC 11 confirms the double listing — same person fought under two identities

places_of_interest.name: The Betting Board
places_of_interest.description: A magically updated odds board at the Betting Halls entrance showing live fight odds. Obsidian Lotus manages the board. Nobody publicly questions the odds.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Insight DC 16 to detect manipulation; caught cheating the board means instant Lotus attention

small_shops.name: Fighter's Row Armament
small_shops.description: Arena-grade weapons sold and maintained. Nets, tridents, gladiuses, and fighting shields. Also does field repairs between matches.
small_shops.signature_item: Gladiatorial net (modified, counts as net weapon)
small_shops.dnd_relevance: net, trident, shield, shortsword arena spec

small_shops.name: The Bone Doctor's Stall
small_shops.description: Unlicensed medic operating between the barracks. Healer's kits, bone setting, and emergency potions. No records kept.
small_shops.dnd_relevance: healer's kit, potions of healing, stabilization

small_shops.name: Razorthorn Blades
small_shops.description: Combat daggers, rapiers, and paired short blades. Silver coating available. All balanced for arena use.
small_shops.dnd_relevance: silvered weapons, dagger, rapier, short swords

Scrapworks.description: Industrial salvage district. Mara the Scrapper's territory.

notable_establishments.name: Mara's Office
notable_establishments.description: The Scrapper runs her operation from here

places_of_interest.name: The Scrap Tower
places_of_interest.description: A sixty-foot tower of salvaged materials — metal, stone, glass — that serves as Mara's observation post and unofficial territory marker. It should not be structurally sound. It is.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Climbing (Athletics DC 12) provides a view across Rings 3-4; acts as a Warden signal relay during emergencies

places_of_interest.name: The Rust Maze Entrance
places_of_interest.description: The above-ground entry to the Rust Maze below — a marked hole in the floor of the main yard covered with a salvaged iron grate. Mara charges 5 EC admission for explorers.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Dungeon entrance — DC 14 Survival to navigate; the maze contains salvage worth 2d6 x 10 EC with a full exploration

places_of_interest.name: The Golem Yard
places_of_interest.description: A separate section of Scrapworks where golem parts and construct components are sorted. Several partial golems stand inert. One of them moved last winter. Nobody investigated.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Arcana DC 14 to identify usable golem components; golem parts worth 50-200 EC each to the right buyer

small_shops.name: Grapple & Grind
small_shops.description: Salvage-quality thieves' tools, climbing gear, grappling hooks, and rope. Everything tested before it leaves the yard.
small_shops.signature_item: Grappling Hook and 50ft rope (salvage quality, 8 EC)
small_shops.dnd_relevance: thieves' tools, climbing gear, grappling hook, rope

small_shops.name: Recycler's Workshop
small_shops.description: Repaired and reconditioned mundane gear — swords straightened, armour re-riveted, tools sharpened. No magic work. Honest prices.
small_shops.signature_item: Armour repair service (any non-magic armour, 5-15 EC)
small_shops.dnd_relevance: equipment maintenance, tool repair

small_shops.name: The Parts Pile
small_shops.description: Golem components, construct materials, and mechanical curiosities sold by Mara's crew. No questions on intended use.
small_shops.signature_item: Partial golem core (salvaged, 100 EC, Arcana DC 12 to use)
small_shops.dnd_relevance: construct components, arcane materials, golem repair

parks.name: The Sorting Floor Garden
parks.description: A small corner of the sorting floors where workers installed a mushroom garden — partly for food, partly because someone said it was good for morale. It has spread significantly.

Artisan Quarter.description: Craftspeople, artists, and the Guild of Ashen Scrolls scriptorium.

places_of_interest.name: The Ashen Scriptorium
places_of_interest.description: The main Guild of Ashen Scrolls scribing facility. Forty scribes work here daily producing scroll copies, illuminated manuscripts, and official records. The smell of ink and preservation wax is permanent.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Scroll scribing services available here at Guild rates; copying spells into spellbooks 20% cheaper than standard

places_of_interest.name: Jeweler's Row Display Windows
places_of_interest.description: The shop-front windows of Jeweler's Row are the most beautiful street-view in Ring 3. Gem-cutters display their best work under magelights. Several items in the windows have been there for years, too expensive to sell.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Gems required for identify, revivify, and raise dead purchased here at standard prices

places_of_interest.name: The Potter's Hall Kiln
places_of_interest.description: The communal kiln serving the entire Potter's Lane collective. Large enough to stand in. Several notable forgeries have been traced to objects that passed through this kiln.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Investigation DC 14 of fired pottery can detect if it was used to conceal or transport contraband

small_shops.name: Inkwright's Scriptorium
small_shops.description: Custom scroll scribing — any spell up to 5th level with 3-day lead. Pre-made combat utility scrolls in stock: haste, hold person, counterspell.
small_shops.signature_item: Scroll of Haste (standard price + 10% scribing fee)
small_shops.dnd_relevance: spell scroll scribing, haste, hold person, counterspell, identify

small_shops.name: Ferric & Sons Armaments
small_shops.description: Three generations of blades. Shortswords, longswords, and hand crossbows to Guild spec. +1 enchantment upgrade service available.
small_shops.dnd_relevance: +1 weapons, shortsword, longsword, hand crossbow

small_shops.name: The Gem Cutter's Standard
small_shops.description: Cut and mounted gemstones for magical use, jewelry, and spell component requirements. Guild of Ashen Scrolls certified.
small_shops.dnd_relevance: diamond dust, spell component gems, identify requirements

parks.name: The Artisan's Courtyard
parks.description: A communal outdoor workspace in the Quarter's center where artisans set up for weather-permitting work. Bioluminescent moss covers the walls, providing soft working light that the artisans claim is better for color judgment.

malls.name: The Quarter Arcade
malls.description: A covered craftsperson's market in the Artisan Quarter running daily from mid-morning to late evening. More curated than Cobbleway — everything here is made, not traded.
malls.specialty: Handcrafted goods, weapons, scrolls, and fine materials

places_of_interest.name: The Hearthstone Memorial
places_of_interest.description: A bronze relief panel on the Community Hall exterior depicting the district's founding — thirty-two families who built the first houses here. Most residents claim to be descended from at least one family.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: History DC 10 to identify a specific founding family; one lineage has an unresolved inheritance case worth 2,000 EC

places_of_interest.name: The Community Well
places_of_interest.description: The central shared well of Hearthstone, pre-dating the canal system. Still functional. Families bring disputes to be resolved 'at the Well' as a tradition.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: The well feeds from an underground source; Zone of Truth effect lingers near the well (DC 12 Wisdom save) from generations of dispute resolution rituals

small_shops.name: The Amber Flask
small_shops.description: Standard, Greater, and Superior Healing Potions. No Guild markup, no questions. Behind the Copper Market, third stall past the lantern post.
small_shops.dnd_relevance: potion of healing, potion of greater healing

small_shops.name: Hearthstone Hardware
small_shops.description: Mundane tools, repair supplies, and household equipment. Also stocks climbing gear and rope as 'household supplies'.
small_shops.dnd_relevance: rope, climbing gear, mundane tools

small_shops.name: The Corner Chirurgeon
small_shops.description: A licensed healer serving Hearthstone families. Mundane medicine, healer's kits, and basic remedy supplies. Affordable rates.
small_shops.dnd_relevance: healer's kit, medicine check assistance, stabilization

parks.name: Hearthstone Common
parks.description: The central green of the district — a rare underground space with dome-light panels providing diffuse daylight-equivalent illumination. Children play here. Families picnic. It is aggressively normal.
features: maintained grass and soil garden beds

parks.name: The Fernway
parks.description: A covered walkway between two residential blocks planted with potted ferns and dim bioluminescent lanterns. Used for morning walks and quiet evenings.

malls.name: Hearthstone Market Square
malls.description: The district's main commercial area — a compact, practical shopping square with general goods, food, and services. Nothing extravagant. Reliably open and reliably stocked.
malls.specialty: Daily goods, household supplies, and basic adventuring consumables

Ember Ward.description: Working class district. Union halls, mutual aid networks.

places_of_interest.name: The Strike Pillar
places_of_interest.description: A salvaged factory pillar at the Union Hall entrance etched with the dates and outcomes of every major labor action in the Ward's history. Wins are carved deep. Losses are carved shallow.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: History DC 10 to count the losses — there are more than the wins; the pillar tells a different story than the Hall's official history

places_of_interest.name: The Aid Cache Wall
places_of_interest.description: A public wall where citizens post anonymous requests for assistance and Patchwork Saints volunteers post anonymous offers. The system is informal and largely functional.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Successful Insight DC 12 identifies which posts are legitimate and which are planted by faction recruiters

small_shops.name: Patchwork Pharmacy
small_shops.description: Saints-run, community-priced. Healer's kits, bandages, herbalism kit supplies, and unlabelled potions of healing. Sliding scale pricing.
small_shops.signature_item: Potion of Healing (sliding scale, 20-50 EC based on means)
small_shops.dnd_relevance: healer's kit, herbalism kit, potions of healing

small_shops.name: The Worker's Tool Shed
small_shops.description: Tools, work supplies, and practical equipment. Also stocks thieves' tools under the counter for union members handling 'labor disputes'.
small_shops.signature_item: Thieves' Tools (under counter, 15 EC, union member only)
small_shops.dnd_relevance: thieves' tools, artisan's tools, work equipment

parks.name: The Commons
parks.description: The Ward's central shared space — an underground park maintained by volunteer labor. Thermal vents from the Ironworks run beneath it, keeping the ground warm year-round. Used for community meetings, informal markets, and rest.

Coppergate.description: Lower middle class. Aspiring merchants and small business owners.

places_of_interest.name: The Copper Arch
places_of_interest.description: A corroded copper archway marking the main entrance to Coppergate from Ring 3. Originally built as a prestige project. The copper was never polished and the green corrosion became the district symbol.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Widely recognized navigation landmark; investigation of the arch reveals several carved initials — some belonging to known criminals

places_of_interest.name: The Hidden Market Signs
places_of_interest.description: Coppergate's unofficial hidden market is signposted by chalk marks and scraped symbols on building corners. Different symbols indicate different goods. The code changes monthly.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Thieves' Tools / Thieves' Cant DC 13 to decode; grants access to the Coppergate Cellars hidden market

small_shops.name: Vault & Rivet
small_shops.description: Studded leather to half-plate fitted same-day. The most practical armour shop in Ring 4.
small_shops.signature_item: Studded Leather Armour (45 EC, same-day fit)
small_shops.dnd_relevance: studded leather, chain shirt, half-plate, shield

small_shops.name: The Careful Hand
small_shops.description: Lockpicks, trap-finding kits, disguise supplies, and forgery components. Sold as 'novelty items' under Coppergate ordinance 7-C.
small_shops.dnd_relevance: thieves' tools, disguise kit, forgery kit

small_shops.name: The Budget Blade
small_shops.description: Secondhand weapons at honest prices. Some of them work. Most of them work. All of them have been used.
small_shops.dnd_relevance: shortsword, dagger, light crossbow (budget quality)

parks.name: The Tenement Yard
parks.description: A shared courtyard between the tenement blocks with a small bioluminescent mushroom patch and a community water pump. Children play here. Laundry hangs overhead.

malls.name: The Copper Market Hall
malls.description: A secondhand and budget goods market covering most of Shop Row — repurposed warehouse with vendor stalls. Everything is either used, surplus, or slightly irregular. Prices are honest.
malls.specialty: Budget equipment, secondhand goods, and practical supplies for working-class residents

Ashfall Terraces.description: Vertical housing built into volcanic slopes. Warm, smoky.

sub_areas.name: Lower Vents
sub_areas.description: Near volcanic activity, cheap but dangerous

places_of_interest.name: The Magma Shrine
places_of_interest.description: A carved stone shrine to the volcanic god Ashara built at a lava tube observation point. Open-flame offerings left here are said to receive volcanic blessings.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Fire domain clerics who make an offering here can cast fire-related spells without spell slots once per long rest (1st-2nd level only)

places_of_interest.name: The Thermal Baths
places_of_interest.description: Natural hot springs in the lava tubes expanded and maintained as public baths. Cheapest hot water in the city. Popular with off-duty Wardens and Ironworks workers.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Long rests taken in the Thermal Baths reduce exhaustion by 2 levels instead of 1 (heat therapy)

places_of_interest.name: The Vent Community
places_of_interest.description: The lowest-rent housing in Ashfall — hovels literally built against volcanic vent openings. Warm, cheap, and occasionally subjected to ash bursts. The residents consider this acceptable.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Constitution DC 10 per hour in the Lower Vents to avoid being subjected to 1 level of exhaustion from heat

small_shops.name: The Ashfall Forge
small_shops.description: Weapons forged at volcanic vent heat — exceptionally tempered. Heat-treating service also available for existing blades.
small_shops.signature_item: Heat-tempered longsword (+1 damage vs cold creatures, 180 EC)
small_shops.dnd_relevance: weapons with fire-adjacent properties, armor heat-treatment

small_shops.name: The Vent Remedies
small_shops.description: Vent-community healer specializing in smoke inhalation, ash burns, and heat exhaustion. Also makes fire resistance salves.
small_shops.signature_item: Fire Resistance Salve (1 hour resistance to fire damage, 80 EC)
small_shops.dnd_relevance: resistance to fire, healer's kit, burn treatment

parks.name: The Upper Terrace Garden
parks.description: A cultivated garden on the upper terraces using volcanic soil — highly fertile. Residents grow unusual heat-adapted plants here. The view of the lower terraces and dome from here is considered the best in Ring 4.

Duskhollow.description: Perpetual shadow zone. Home to night workers, those who avoid light.

sub_areas.name: The Blind Quarter
sub_areas.description: Where those without sight live comfortably

places_of_interest.name: The Lightless Library
places_of_interest.description: A repository of forbidden texts maintained by an unknown curator — located in Duskhollow Depths. All books are written in Braille or encoded for tactile reading. The curator has never been identified.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Contains texts unavailable anywhere else; finding and reading requires DC 15 Investigation + ability to read without sight (or blindsight)

places_of_interest.name: The Shadow Arch
places_of_interest.description: An archway of dark stone at Duskhollow's entrance where no light penetrates. Not magical — the stone absorbs light. A natural phenomenon the community treats as sacred.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Magical darkness passes through this archway unimpeded; light spells fail to illuminate it

places_of_interest.name: The Night Market Square
places_of_interest.description: The Night Market's central plaza where vendors sell after dark exclusively. Bioluminescent markers on the ground guide navigation. Non-darkvision visitors frequently lose their footing.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Disadvantage on Perception checks without darkvision; Night Market items rotate but always include contraband at 10% off standard black market rates

small_shops.name: Under the Counter
small_shops.description: Everything the Guild doesn't officially sell. Poisons, smoke bombs, caltrops, and dust of disappearance. Night Market hours only. No Warden tokens. No credit.
small_shops.dnd_relevance: basic poison, smoke bomb, caltrops, dust of disappearance

small_shops.name: Duskweave Tailors
small_shops.description: Arcane-threaded robes and spell-resistant leathers. Silence-treated soles, mage-stitched pockets, and a lining that won't betray you under detect magic.
small_shops.signature_item: Silence-treated leather boots (Stealth check advantage, 120 EC)
small_shops.dnd_relevance: stealth-enhanced armor, mage armor equivalent, detect magic resistant clothing

small_shops.name: The Lightless Market
small_shops.description: Night Market general goods — practical supplies sold in the dark. Everything pre-packaged for tactile identification. Surprisingly well-organized.
small_shops.dnd_relevance: low-light tools, non-magical darkvision aids, adventuring supplies

parks.name: The Blind Quarter Garden
parks.description: A garden maintained by Blind Quarter residents that is navigable entirely by touch and scent — textured paths, strongly fragrant plants, and wind chimes at key junctions. No lighting at all.

Outer Wall.description: Warden military installations. Four Great Gates, 12 bastions.

places_of_interest.name: The Warden Tombs
places_of_interest.description: The honored dead of the Wardens interred in the Wall Crypts beneath the Outer Wall. An honor guard of three Wardens rotates through at all times, even during Rift events.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Speak with dead cast here requires DC 14 Religion check — the dead Wardens actively resist questioning about classified operations

places_of_interest.name: The Great Gates
places_of_interest.description: The four massive gates of the Outer Wall — the only official exits from the city. Each is 40 feet tall, enchanted iron and stone. Warden-controlled. Closed since the last major Rift breach.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: knock and arcane lock spells are ineffective; the locks are mechanical with additional ward against magic

places_of_interest.name: The Wall's Edge Observation Posts
places_of_interest.description: Twelve bastions along the Wall with Warden observation posts. Civilians can apply for observation access during daylight — the view of beyond the city is disquieting.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Perception DC 12 from any post reveals Rift scarring on the terrain outside — unusual density near the Dawn Gate

small_shops.name: The Warden's Forge
small_shops.description: Warden-surplus chain mail and splint armour — inspected, repaired, re-fitted. Shield repairs while you wait.
small_shops.dnd_relevance: chain mail, splint armor, shield, armor repair

small_shops.name: The Armory Overflow
small_shops.description: Surplus Warden weapons sold off when inventory rotates. Spears, hand axes, and shortswords in good condition.
small_shops.dnd_relevance: spear, handaxe, shortsword (surplus military spec)

parks.name: The Warden Memorial Garden
parks.description: A small maintained garden between two Wall bastions dedicated to fallen Wardens. Austere and functional. Flowers from every recruit's home district are planted here — a tradition.

Ironworks.description: Iron Fang heavy industry. Factories, foundries, worker housing.

places_of_interest.name: The Iron Fang Smokestacks
places_of_interest.description: The four massive smokestacks of the main Ironworks foundry. Visible from Ring 3 on a clear day. Workers claim the smoke patterns predict the next Rift event. They are sometimes correct.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Perception DC 14 on a given day to interpret smoke patterns; on a successful check, DM rolls twice for next Rift event timing and chooses the worse result

places_of_interest.name: The Furnace Heart
places_of_interest.description: The oldest and largest furnace in the Ironworks — buried in the Industrial Underworks. Workers say it hasn't been fully extinguished since the Consortium's founding. Iron Fang leadership keeps it as a symbol.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Fire elementals have been spotted near the Furnace Heart three times in the last year; Constitution DC 13 per hour in the Underworks near it

small_shops.name: The Iron Covenant
small_shops.description: Weapons forged in Ironworks furnaces. War hammers, battleaxes, and greataxes. No filigree. Consortium workers get 10% off.
small_shops.dnd_relevance: war hammer, battleaxe, greataxe, maul

small_shops.name: The Worker's Store
small_shops.description: Company-run general store for Ironworks workers. Overpriced basics available only to Consortium employees. Also sells industrial safety gear that doubles as light armor.
small_shops.signature_item: Industrial Work Apron (improvised light armor, AC 11)
small_shops.dnd_relevance: improvised armor, industrial tools, basic supplies

Shantytown Heights.description: Vertical slums. Patchwork Saints territory. Poverty but community.

sub_areas.name: Stack Housing
sub_areas.description: Vertical slums built atop each other

places_of_interest.name: The Bridges
places_of_interest.description: Precarious rope and plank walkways between the stack housing towers. Marked with knotted rope signals by Saints members indicating safe/unsafe bridge status.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Athletics DC 12 to cross safely; DC 16 in adverse conditions; failure results in a fall with distance determined by bridge height

places_of_interest.name: Saints' Wall
places_of_interest.description: A plastered wall at the Saints' Refuge entrance covered in hand-painted murals of community members — births, deaths, acts of courage. New panels are added constantly.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Investigation DC 12 identifies a specific person from description; three current missing persons have faces in the mural

small_shops.name: The Dead Weight Supply Co.
small_shops.description: Rope, pitons, torches, iron rations, and ten-foot poles. Delivers to Warrens access points. Keeping the bottom of the city alive.
small_shops.signature_item: Ten-Foot Pole (1 EC, free with purchase of climbing kit)
small_shops.dnd_relevance: rope, pitons, torches, iron rations, ten-foot pole, climbing gear

small_shops.name: The Hidden Clinic
small_shops.description: Unlicensed Saints-run medical care. Healer's kits, basic surgery, and cure wounds potions. No Warden reporting. Ever.
small_shops.dnd_relevance: healer's kit, stabilization, cure wounds (potion)

parks.name: The Deepstack Commons
parks.description: A ground-level open space at the base of the stack housing towers. Technically a park — more of an outdoor community room. Shared cooking, childcare, and Saints organization meetings all happen here simultaneously.

Collapsed Plaza.description: Ruined district from a past Rift disaster. Scavenger territory. Dangerous.

places_of_interest.name: The Rift Scar
places_of_interest.description: The original Rift breach point that destroyed the district — a 30-foot crack in the stone ground that still occasionally bleeds spatial distortion. Warden tape marks a 20-foot exclusion zone that nobody respects.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Wild magic surge check (DC 12 Arcana) for any spell cast within 10ft; wild magic surge table applies on failure

places_of_interest.name: The Broken Sanctum
places_of_interest.description: A partially collapsed temple to an unknown deity that predates the current religious establishment. The Cult of Thane uses the intact sections for initiations. The collapsed sections have not been excavated.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Religion DC 16 to identify the deity; History DC 14 confirms the temple predates all current faction records

places_of_interest.name: The Scavenger's Wall
places_of_interest.description: A section of intact wall in the Rubble Fields where scavengers post trade offers, warnings about specific rubble areas, and maps of cleared zones. Updated nightly.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Investigation DC 11 to find specific relevant information; one posting per visit can be acted on without a Deception check to determine authenticity

small_shops.name: Shadowthread Outfitters
small_shops.description: Cloaks of the Manta Ray, darkvision aids, and black-dyed leathers. Location is not advertised. You know how to find them or you don't.
small_shops.signature_item: Cloak of the Manta Ray (permanent enchant, 500 EC)
small_shops.dnd_relevance: cloak of the manta ray, darkvision tools, stealth equipment

small_shops.name: The Rubble Finder's Post
small_shops.description: Scavenger-run gear depot. Sells salvage tools, mapping equipment, and supplies for exploring the Collapsed Plaza's depths.
small_shops.signature_item: Cartographer's tools (modified for rubble mapping, 12 EC)
small_shops.dnd_relevance: cartographer's tools, climbing gear, rope, rubble-specific exploration gear

The Fringe.description: Edge of mapped territory. Last permanent habitation before the unknown.

places_of_interest.name: The Last Light
places_of_interest.description: The final permanent magelight at the edge of the Last Light Settlement. Beyond it, there is nothing but darkness and Rift territory. Residents treat it as both a monument and a warning.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: light spells cast beyond the Last Light are immediately suppressed by an antimagic effect of unknown origin

places_of_interest.name: The Void Watch Post
places_of_interest.description: A Glass Sigil monitoring station at the absolute edge of mapped territory. Three archivists rotate through on 48-hour shifts. None of them discuss what they have seen. Two previous archivists did not return.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Arcana DC 18 to successfully calibrate monitoring equipment; successful calibration predicts a Rift event within 24h (60% accuracy)

places_of_interest.name: The Edge Marker
places_of_interest.description: A stone post driven into the ground at the furthest mapped point of the city. It has been replaced six times. The current post leans slightly toward the dark.
places_of_interest.dnd_relevance: Detect magic reveals a faint evocation aura from beyond the marker — consistent across all observations, origin unknown

small_shops.name: The Emergency Cache Post
small_shops.description: Glass Sigil-maintained emergency supply post in the Last Light Settlement. Basic survival gear, emergency rations, and Rift-response supplies. Access requires Sigil authorization or genuine emergency.
small_shops.dnd_relevance: Rift exposure countermeasures, emergency rations, climbing gear

warrens_distribution.name: Eastern Warrens
warrens_distribution.description: Oldest warren network. Smugglers, cults, Patchwork Saints stronghold.

warrens_distribution.name: Northern Warrens (The Depths)
warrens_distribution.description: Deepest underground. Mushroom farms, blind communities, forgotten things.

warrens_distribution.name: Western Warrens (Rustside)
warrens_distribution.description: Former industrial. Toxic salvage, dangerous chemicals, desperate communities.

warrens_distribution.name: Southern Warrens (Ashfall)
warrens_distribution.description: Near volcanic vents. Forge communities, heat-adapted peoples.

warrens_distribution.name: Underbelly Warrens
warrens_distribution.description: Vertical slums in the city's foundations. No natural light ever reaches here.

sewers.description: The vast sewer network that serves the entire city. Multiple levels, some areas unmapped.

major_sections.name: Forum Sewers
major_sections.description: Well-maintained, Warden-patrolled. Clean by sewer standards.

major_sections.name: Sanctum Drains
major_sections.description: Holy water runoff creates strange effects. Some areas warded.

major_sections.name: Market Underdrain
major_sections.description: Heavy traffic from commerce. Smuggler routes. Rat problems.

major_sections.name: Residential Collectors
major_sections.description: Standard residential waste. Occasionally used by criminals.

major_sections.name: Industrial Outflow
major_sections.description: Toxic, dangerous, largely unmonitored. Strange mutations.

major_sections.name: Sewer Grid 7
major_sections.description: Rift-affected section. Reality unstable. Glass Sigil monitors.

major_sections.name: The Deep Sewers
major_sections.description: Ancient levels beneath the modern system. No maps exist.

lairs.description: Known creature lairs and monster dens throughout the underground.

locations.name: The Rat King's Warren
locations.description: Massive intelligent rat colony. Trade information for food.
locations.inhabitants: Giant rats, rat-folk, the Rat King himself

locations.name: Slime Pits
locations.description: Toxic pools breeding oozes and slimes of various types.

locations.name: The Spider Galleries
locations.description: Web-choked tunnels home to giant spider colonies.

locations.name: Goblin Warrens
locations.description: Extensive goblin settlement in the deep tunnels.

locations.name: The Carrion Caves
locations.description: Where ghouls and worse feed on the dead.

locations.name: Troll Depths
locations.description: Where trolls regenerate in the dark and hunt.

locations.name: The Wyvern Roost
locations.description: Volcanic caves where fire-resistant wyverns nest.

locations.name: Mimic Alley
locations.description: An entire section where mimics have established dominance.

dungeons.description: Ancient structures, abandoned facilities, and dangerous complexes beneath the city.

locations.name: The Old Prison
locations.description: Pre-Tower era prison complex. Cells still intact. Something still screams at night.
locations.history: Built before the Tower arrived. Used for political prisoners. Sealed after an incident.

locations.name: The Sunken Temple
locations.description: Temple to a forgotten god, collapsed into the underground. Still holy... to something.
locations.history: Predates current pantheon. Collapsed during the Third Rift Crisis.

locations.name: Artificer's Folly
locations.description: Abandoned research complex. Failed golem experiments still patrol.
locations.history: Sealed after a catastrophic experiment 200 years ago.

locations.name: The Merchant Vaults
locations.description: Legendary treasure vaults from the first Merchant Princes. Trapped extensively.
locations.history: Built during the founding era. Keys lost to time.

locations.name: The Warden Tombs
locations.description: Where fallen Wardens are interred. Honor guard still patrols.
locations.history: Sacred burial ground for defenders of the Wall.

locations.name: The Rift Laboratories
locations.description: Research facility built to study Rifts. Abandoned after researchers changed.
locations.history: Tower Authority project, terminated. Records sealed.

locations.name: The Drowned Coliseum
locations.description: Ancient arena from a civilization before the Tower. Partially flooded.

locations.name: Thane's Labyrinth
locations.description: Tunnel complex being excavated by Brother Thane's Cult. Purpose unknown.
locations.history: Currently under construction. The Cult guards it jealously.

sanctums.description: Hidden holy places, cult strongholds, and secret gathering places.

locations.name: The Choir Undercroft
locations.description: Secret Serpent Choir meeting hall. Divine contracts too sensitive for surface.

locations.name: Thane's Inner Sanctum
locations.description: Brother Thane's true seat of power. Where the Returned truly gather.
locations.access: Trusted cult members, Speakers and above

locations.name: The Widow's Web
locations.description: Obsidian Lotus true headquarters. The Widow rules from here.

locations.name: The Memory Vault
locations.description: Glass Sigil's most sensitive storage. Memories deemed too dangerous to exist.

locations.name: Saints' Refuge
locations.description: Secret Patchwork Saints headquarters and emergency shelter.

locations.name: The Forge Shrine
locations.description: Secret shrine to Ashara the Phoenix Marshal. Wardens' hidden faith.
locations.access: Wardens who know the old ways

locations.name: The Counting House
locations.description: Iron Fang's true vault and meeting room. Where real deals happen.

locations.name: The Arena Crypts
locations.description: Where Argent Blades initiate new members through blood trials.

locations.name: The Silent Library
locations.description: Repository of forbidden texts maintained by an unknown curator.

locations.name: The Tower's Roots
locations.description: Ancient chambers at the Tower's foundation. The Oracle's dreams echo here.

transit_tunnels.description: The underground transit network connecting districts.

locations.name: Deep Line Stations
locations.description: Unofficial underground train connecting warren clusters. No Warden patrols.

locations.name: Maintenance Tunnels
locations.description: Service tunnels for the legitimate train lines. Worker access only.

locations.name: Abandoned Stations
locations.description: Old stations from routes no longer in service.

special_underground.description: Unique underground locations that don't fit other categories.

locations.name: Echo Alley
locations.description: Acoustically haunted smuggler tunnels. Sound behaves wrong. Obsidian Lotus territory.

locations.name: The Fungal Forest
locations.description: Massive underground mushroom forest. Food source for deep communities.

locations.name: The Crystalline Caves
locations.description: Natural crystal formations with magical resonance.

locations.name: The Bone Market
locations.description: Underground black market dealing in remains, relics, and forbidden goods.

locations.name: The Drowning Pools
locations.description: Flooded chambers with air pockets. Aquatic creatures and worse.

locations.name: Rift Scar Zone
locations.description: Areas permanently damaged by Rift activity. Reality is thin.

train_tubes.description: Seven major tube lines connecting the city.

major_lines.name: Spine Line (Silver)
major_lines.route: Tower → Forum → Sanctum → Markets → North Wall

major_lines.name: Eastern Radial (Blue)
major_lines.route: Forum → Sanctum East → Markets East → Hearthstone → Eastern Warrens

major_lines.name: Northern Radial (White)
major_lines.route: Forum → Temple Row → Floating Bazaar → Ashfall → Fringe

major_lines.name: Southern Radial (Green)
major_lines.route: Forum → Guild Spires → Scrapworks → Collapsed Plaza → Southern Warrens

canal_rings.name: Forum Canal
canal_rings.description: Separates Forum from Sanctum. Diplomatic vessels.

canal_rings.name: Outer Canal (The Trench)
canal_rings.description: Industrial shipping, military patrols, smugglers at night.
